text:
Nils Lundkvist has become a bigger part of Dallas's blue line than his career line suggests. He's up to 20 minutes a night over the last 10 games, more than two and a half minutes above his season average, with five points in that stretch. His goal against Vegas last week was his first of the season.

The points are mostly assists (seven of eight), and that's his game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him at 6.1 primary shot assists per 60, 88th percentile among defensemen; watch where the puck goes when he has it in the offensive zone. He barely shoots for himself (0.14 expected goals per 60), and his on-ice results are a touch unlucky: Dallas has scored 2.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there.

The bigger case is defensive. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.1 wins above replacement last season, 63rd among defensemen, mostly from even-strength defense, with opponents getting fewer chances when he played. The Stars take 53.5% of the expected goals at five on five with him on this season. The 2018 first-round pick of the Rangers is finally playing like one.
